mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring any specific threshold condition.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS is rising, or the correlation between RSAFS growth and SPX returns is less than 0.1 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that reduces liquidity and increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the average 5-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and rise in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of UNRATE decline and PAYEMS rise fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression of SPX returns on UNRATE and PAYEMS is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity, which precedes a recession and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO declines, or the correlation between INDPRO decline and negative SPX returns is less than -0.2 in the late-cycle regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates rising inflation, which typically leads to central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring a specific threshold.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL is rising, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL growth and SPX returns is greater than -0.1 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1400 thousand units for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer wealth and corporate revenues, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the average 5-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), a decline in the unemployment rate signals improving labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of high-unemployment periods when UNRATE declines, or the correlation between UNRATE decline and SPX returns is less than 0.1 in the high-unemployment regime.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer and housing demand, which drives corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of RSAFS and HOUST increases fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression of SPX returns on RSAFS and HOUST is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
